neet_che_u04_t04_2.working: For a monoatomic gas Cp = 5/2 R. q = nCpΔT = 2 × 2.5 × 8.314 × 50 = 2078.5 J ≈ 2.08 kJ

neet_che_u04_t04_3.working: For a diatomic gas Cv = 5/2 R. ΔU = nCvΔT = 3 × (5/2)R × 20 = 150R, regardless of the process.

neet_che_u04_t04_4.working: A is true: the coffee-cup calorimeter works at constant pressure (q = ΔH), the bomb calorimeter at constant volume (q = ΔU). R is true: Cp − Cv = R. R does not explain A; A follows from the constant P vs constant V conditions.

neet_che_u04_t04_5.working: I is false: for an ideal gas, ΔU = nCvΔT holds for any process. II is true: Cp = 7/2 R, so q = 1 × 3.5R × 10 = 35R.
